content.text: No minimum-commitment or take-or-pay mechanic exists anywhere in the fee architecture. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Corio to pay Commerce One [*] of all Application Management Revenue from Corio Customers for use of Commerce One Software or MarketSite.net Service Access subject to the following limitations.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase or volume commitment on Corio and meets the preferred position. Exhibit B prices Software Users as "Unlimited" (p0151), the licence fee is a one-time amount due on Software Acceptance (p0152, p0165), and the MarketSite.net access and maintenance fees are annual fees for services actually made available (p0153, p0154, p0168), with maintenance continuing only "provided that Corio continues to pay" (p0055) rather than being a guaranteed spend. Variable fees track actual activity: Application Management Revenue share is a percentage of revenue actually invoiced to Corio Customers (p0157) and implementation work is on a time-and-materials basis capped at a stated maximum (p0161); further professional services and training arise only at Corio's request and by mutual agreement (p0068, p0067). There is no committed user count, no minimum guarantee, no take-or-pay and no shortfall penalty. Two points noted but not flagged: the 40-Authorized-Software-User "minimum limitation" in p0158 is a qualifying condition for the royalty-free use of the initial 3000 licences, not a purchase obligation or usage cap; and the "shortfall" reference in the audit clause (p0059) is a reciprocal true-up of under/overpayments, which is expressly the treatment our playbook prefers. Accordingly no redline is proposed.
